workLog.entry: Swept the 12 open issues and pulled each body plus its full comment thread. Verified live rather than trusting the reports: Copilot CLI is 1.0.75 here, and an edit-tool probe against a scratch file succeeded, which disproves the standing report in issue #3316.

Checked the ruff enforcement surface for #2993. Every lefthook ruff step passes --exit-zero and the pre-push one is even named python-lint-advisory, so ruff blocks nothing locally. The blocking gate is the changed-file ratchet in the Python Tests workflow. Found scripts/ci/ruff_count_ratchet.py, written for the #2993 regression-guard criterion with a full test file, and grep showed nothing invokes it anywhere in .github, lefthook, or scripts. Same for scripts/ci/adr006_run_block_scanner.py and its --max ratchet mode, written for #2967. Two tested gates, zero enforcement.

Ran the count ratchet locally: it claimed 767 violations against a baseline of 408 and reported a regression. The real tracked-file count is 361. Cause: it invokes ruff check . with a single hardcoded exclude, so it walks untracked nested worktrees and scratch trees that happen to be on disk. Replaced the directory walk with a git ls-files scan over tracked .py paths, chunked to a 24000-byte argv budget so the roughly 70 KB path list stays under the Windows 32767-char CreateProcess ceiling. The rewritten scan reproduced 361 exactly, matching the independent manual count.

Lowered the baseline from 408 to 361 to lock in drain that had already happened but was never recorded. Extended the test file from 8 to 14 cases: the shared subprocess fake now answers both the git and ruff legs, plus a git-failure external-error case, an empty-tracked-set case, a multi-batch accumulation case that fails if batches overwrite instead of summing, an argv-budget property check, an oversized-single-path case, and a real-git integration test that builds a repo with one clean tracked file next to an untracked directory full of violations and asserts the count is zero.

Wired both gates. The count ratchet runs in the Python Tests workflow beside the existing changed-file ratchet, under the same python-changed gate, since ruff debt only moves when Python moves. The ADR-006 run-block ratchet runs in the PR Validation workflow at --max 87, because workflow YAML can change in any PR and the Python Tests workflow skips when no Python changed. Both are single-line invocations of a tested script, so neither adds logic to workflow YAML and the scanner still reports 87 after the edit.

nextSteps: Drain the 361 ruff violations opportunistically and lower the baseline with --update after each cleanup.
Extract one large ADR-006 run block per PR and lower --max to match; the two biggest are in the ai-review composite action at 142 and 117 code lines.
Consider whether the pre-push python-lint-advisory step should become blocking now that whole-tree growth is gated, since the advisory step is the reason contributors do not see ruff debt until CI.
